introduction: How would one recognize a Messenger of God? The readings set miracles aside as proof only for those who saw them and name others: the Person, the revealed Word that none can imitate, the deeds, the fulfilment of earlier scripture, and above all the education of whole peoples by one who had no schooling, no army and, in Bahá’u’lláh’s case, no freedom. The Báb and Bahá’u’lláh press one argument repeatedly on believers in earlier religions: the proof you accepted then is the proof offered now. The Gospels and the Qur’án show the same debate in their own day: the demand for signs, “never man spake like this man,” “produce a surah the like thereof,” “is not this the carpenter?” They are joined here by Deuteronomy’s and Jeremiah’s tests of a prophet, Gamaliel’s counsel, Maimonides and Carlyle. The sceptics are heard as well: Hume on testimony and on rival religions, Paine on revelation as hearsay, Clifford on evidence, Newton and the Talmud on confident readers of prophecy, and the Buddha, Emerson and Whitman, who looked for the light within.
questions: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá calls the education and progress of a people “the sure proof,” and Jesus says “by their fruits.” Swift observed that believers have just enough religion to hate. How should the fruits of a religion be judged?
Miracles are set aside as proof for eyewitnesses only. Compare the reasons given by ‘Abdu’l-Bahá, the Qur’án, Maimonides and Hume. Where do they agree?
“His proof is His own Self,” and next His Word. Paine replies that revelation is hearsay to everyone but the first hearer. What can a person who comes centuries later examine for himself?

The Báb and Bahá’u’lláh ask: by what proof did you accept your own religion? Hume says the evidences of different religions destroy one another. What must be true for one kind of proof to serve several Messengers?
The Bereans tested Paul by the scriptures they had; the Kitáb-i-Aqdas says the Book is itself the Balance. How does an honest inquirer use what he already believes without being imprisoned by it?

The last readings ask the friends to learn the proofs and “speak out,” and the First Letter of Peter hopes that some will be won “without the word.” What part do argument, conduct and a person’s own discovery each play in recognition?

outside.why: The proof is “the cultivation of heavenly attributes in the hearts and lives of His followers.” Jesus gave the same test: ye shall know them by their fruits.
“The penetration and potency of His Word.” Officers sent to arrest Jesus came back without him and gave their reason: never man spake like this man.

Sense, reason, tradition and inspiration are each called faulty. The Buddha told the Kalamas much the same and then named what remains: when you know for yourselves. What does ‘Abdu’l-Bahá put in the place of the four?

All four human standards of judgment are found wanting. W. K. Clifford drew the opposite conclusion from human fallibility: it is wrong always, everywhere, and for anyone, to believe anything upon insufficient evidence. What would count as sufficient for him, and for the readings?
Whoever advances a claim must “support his assertions with clear proofs.” God in Isaiah demands the same of the idols: produce your cause; bring forth your strong reasons.
“The sure proof … is in the education and progress of the people.” Luke: every tree is known by his own fruit.

A religion “can hardly be evaluated by the acts of those who only claim to follow” it. Swift, a clergyman, on his fellow believers: we have just enough religion to make us hate, but not enough to make us love one another. If fruits are the proof, which fruits may be set aside?
“One sanctified Soul revives the world of humanity.” Isaiah: the people that walked in darkness have seen a great light.
He “develops the minds, quickens the souls.” The Qur’án on what a Messenger does: to recite unto them His revelations and to make them grow, and to teach them the Scripture and wisdom.
Miracles are “the proofs sought by the uninformed masses.” Jesus to a nobleman: except ye see signs and wonders, ye will not believe.
Marvels “do not constitute a conclusive proof.” Maimonides laid down the same for the awaited Messiah: one should not presume that he must work miracles and wonders.

A miracle convinces only those who saw it. Hume gave the sceptic’s reason: no testimony is sufficient to establish a miracle unless its falsehood would be more miraculous than the fact. Do Hume and ‘Abdu’l-Bahá set miracles aside for the same reason?
The limit of the spectacular. Abraham in the parable: if they hear not Moses and the prophets, neither will they be persuaded, though one rose from the dead.
The sun “needeth no proof”; it is the blind who ask for one. A man born blind, pressed by the authorities for an argument: one thing I know, that, whereas I was blind, now I see.
One appeared two thousand years ago “and His effects still persist.” Isaiah: my word shall not return unto me void, but it shall accomplish that which I please.
“The first and foremost testimony establishing His truth is His own Self.” Jesus: though I bear record of myself, yet my record is true: for I know whence I came, and whither I go.
His own Self is the first testimony. In the same Gospel Jesus also says: if I bear witness of myself, my witness is not true. How can both sayings stand, and what does the second add to the first?

“My proof is Mine own Being … and that which floweth from My pen.” The Qur’án: what thing is of most weight in testimony? Allah is Witness between me and you, and this Qur’án hath been inspired in me.

None knows this “save those who have turned with sanctified countenance.” Jesus makes knowing depend on the same turning: if any man will do his will, he shall know of the doctrine, whether it be of God.
The hidden God “can never be known except through His Manifestation.” John: no man hath seen God at any time; the only begotten Son, he hath declared him.

No greater proof than “His own Person.” Paine objected that a person can be proof only to those who met him: it is revelation to the first person only, and hearsay to every other. How do the readings answer for those who come later?
“My proof is My Self, and My evidence that which hath appeared from Me.” Jesus: though ye believe not me, believe the works.
He stood forth “amidst the concourse of Mine enemies.” Paul before a king appeals to the same publicity: this thing was not done in a corner.
“My deeds sufficient witness to that which issueth from My mouth.” Jesus: the same works that I do bear witness of me.

“Weigh not the Book of God with such standards and sciences as are current amongst you.” The Bereans are praised for weighing Paul’s message by the scriptures they had: they searched the scriptures daily, whether those things were so. When is testing a new word by an old book fair, and when is it the error named here?
“These utterances themselves proclaim the true nature of the Faith.” The Letter to the Hebrews on what such a word does: quick, and powerful, and sharper than any twoedged sword.
The supreme proof is the revelation of verses, “beyond the power of all dwellers on earth to produce the like.” The Báb refers to this challenge in the Qur’án: produce a surah of the like thereof.
The same challenge at full stretch: though mankind and the jinn should assemble to produce the like of this Qur’án, they could not.
Part of the argument is who spoke the verses. The Qur’án of Muḥammad: thou wast not a reader of any scripture before it, nor didst thou write it with thy right hand.
The same wonder was felt in Jerusalem: how knoweth this man letters, having never learned? Jesus answered, my doctrine is not mine, but his that sent me.

“By the same proof through which thou didst become faithful to the religion of the Qur’án.” The Qur’án had said it of an earlier people: when there cometh unto them a scripture confirming that in their possession, they disbelieve therein.
“Bring forth a book like unto this Tablet.” The Qur’án: or they say, he hath invented it. Say: then bring ten surahs, the like thereof, invented.
God adduced no proof for Muḥammad “save your inability to produce the verses.” When portents were demanded, the Qur’án’s answer was: portents are with Allah only, and I am but a plain warner.

Raised among the Persians, a merchant, and then the verses came. Amos to the priest who told him to go home: I was no prophet, neither was I a prophet’s son; but I was an herdman, and the Lord took me.
Whoever cannot speak so without reflection should seek forgiveness. Jeremiah’s test between the dreamer and the one who has the word: what is the chaff to the wheat? Is not my word like as a fire?

“My proof is none other than that proof whereby the truth of the Prophet Muḥammad was established.” The Qur’án: now hath a proof from your Lord come unto you, and We have sent down unto you a clear light.

If the Qur’án proves Muḥammad, the writings of Bahá’u’lláh prove him. Hume argued that the evidences of different religions cancel one another: in matters of religion, whatever is different is contrary. What would Hume have to accept before one proof could serve for several Messengers?
“One word or one verse … is sufficient proof.” The crowd after the Sermon on the Mount: he taught them as one having authority, and not as the scribes.

Visions are no proof, and in eloquence the Báb can outdo any rival. Paul refuses to rest on eloquence at all: not with enticing words of man’s wisdom, but in demonstration of the Spirit and of power. What is the difference between the power of the Word and skill with words?
The Báb quotes the Qur’án. Here is the verse: is it not enough for them that We have sent down unto thee the Scripture which is read unto them?
A prince demanded evidence, and the verses are named as conclusive. The crowd to Jesus: what sign shewest thou then, that we may see, and believe thee?
Let them send representatives “on condition that they possess their own eyes and ears.” Philip to a doubtful Nathanael: come and see.
“The proofs applicable to one Prophet are equally applicable to another.” Deuteronomy gave Israel a test meant for every prophet to come: how shall we know the word which the Lord hath not spoken?
“If ye deny this Cause … by what proof can ye establish that which ye possess?” Jesus: had ye believed Moses, ye would have believed me.
“By what proof can ye establish that which ye claim?” Asked for his authority, Jesus asked the priests about John the Baptist, and they could not answer without undoing their own position.
“By what proof did ye believe in God’s Messengers of old?” The Qur’án: even thus, as they now speak, spake those who were before them. Their hearts are all alike.
“An emigrant” who founded a nation. The call to Abraham: get thee out of thy country, and from thy kindred, and from thy father’s house.
“A man who was a stammerer.” Moses himself: O my Lord, I am not eloquent; I am slow of speech, and of a slow tongue.
“A young merchant” became a universal Educator. The Qur’án: the Prophet who can neither read nor write.

“A fact that no fair-minded person can deny.” Carlyle, lecturing to a Christian audience in 1840, on Muḥammad: the lies which well-meaning zeal has heaped round this man are disgraceful to ourselves only.
He “advanced His Cause from within the Most Great Prison.” Paul from prison: the things which happened unto me have fallen out rather unto the furtherance of the gospel.
No army, no office, a prison cell. Zechariah: not by might, nor by power, but by my spirit, saith the Lord of hosts.

A prisoner whose fame encircled the world. A Cavalier poet in an English gaol found freedom inside himself: stone walls do not a prison make. How is the prisoner’s inner freedom different from the proof ‘Abdu’l-Bahá sees in this imprisonment?
The Cause is “more manifest than to need proof.” Asked to say plainly who he was, Jesus replied: I told you, and ye believed not: the works that I do in my Father’s name, they bear witness of me.
A list of signs offered to an honest question. John the Baptist sent from prison to ask, art thou he that should come? Jesus answered with what could be seen and heard.
They held “the Proof as supreme, and the evidence as outweighing traditions.” Jesus: laying aside the commandment of God, ye hold the tradition of men.

Tradition is the branch; the proof is the root. The rabbis open their Ethics with tradition as the root itself: Moses received the Torah at Sinai and transmitted it to Joshua, Joshua to the elders. What is lost, and what is risked, when tradition is made to give way?
Four proofs, the first being prophecy. Jeremiah’s rule: when the word of the prophet shall come to pass, then shall the prophet be known.
Prophecy, words, deeds, teachings. Jesus offers his hearers a choice of grounds: believe me, or else believe me for the very works’ sake.

“The proof is not of one kind only, but of all kinds.” Pascal thought the decisive kind was none of the arguable ones: the heart has its reasons, which reason does not know. Which kind of proof has actually moved the people you know?
In past ages “the ignorant found grounds for hesitation” in the letter of prophecy. Jerusalem: we know this man whence he is: but when Christ cometh, no man knoweth whence he is.
The Sun shone “from behind subtle clouds.” Nazareth: is not this the carpenter, the son of Mary? And they were offended at him.
“Every proof and prophecy” is centred in two persons. Matthew’s Gospel argues in the same way, verse after verse: that it might be fulfilled which was spoken by the prophet.

Prophecy is claimed as fulfilled. Newton, who spent years on Daniel and Revelation, warned against the confidence of interpreters: the folly of interpreters has been to foretell times and things by this prophecy. How is recognizing a fulfilment different from predicting one?
“The Sacred Scriptures testify.” Jesus: search the scriptures; they are they which testify of me.
Everything foretold, “and notwithstanding, they have arisen to turn away.” Jesus over Jerusalem: thou knewest not the time of thy visitation.
The proof of Moses was his staff; the proof now is the Pen. The scene referred to: Aaron’s rod swallowed up their rods.
The heaven is cleft and the mountains scattered, and few have noticed. Jesus: ye can discern the face of the sky; but can ye not discern the signs of the times?

“The proof hath been completed.” The rabbis of the Talmud distrusted every announcement that the end had come: may those who calculate the end of days be cursed, for when the date passes people say he will never come. How should a claim of fulfilment be tested by people who share that caution?

The Bearer must be of the Prophet’s lineage, “free from physical defects that would repel hearts,” dignified. Isaiah’s servant has none of the outward marks: he hath no form nor comeliness; there is no beauty that we should desire him. What weight should outward qualifications carry?

The outward path lists descent and bearing. Samuel, choosing a king among Jesse’s sons, was told: man looketh on the outward appearance, but the Lord looketh on the heart. Why does the Báb offer an “outward path” as well?

“In what revelation, after God and His signs, will they then believe?” A psalm from a ruined Jerusalem gives the voice of those who would believe and see nothing: we see not our signs: there is no more any prophet. What do the readings say to that complaint?
“We will show them Our signs in the horizons and in themselves.” The nineteenth psalm: the heavens declare the glory of God; day unto day uttereth speech.

Signs in the horizons and in the self. Whitman found them without any messenger: I find letters from God dropt in the street, and every one is sign’d by God’s name. If signs are everywhere, why is an Educator still needed?
“The blind ones say, Where is this manifest light?” Jesus: if ye were blind, ye should have no sin: but now ye say, We see; therefore your sin remaineth.
“Is there one endowed with the sense of smell … one possessed of sight?” The proof is offered to the senses of the heart. A psalm: O taste and see that the Lord is good.
Let the doubter come, hear, and “be an eye-witness of the clear proof.” Paul: prove all things; hold fast that which is good.
“Hast thou heard of a Revelation more mighty than this?” Jesus made a claim as large for his own words: heaven and earth shall pass away, but my words shall not pass away.
“To what face will ye turn today?” Elijah on Carmel: how long halt ye between two opinions? And the people answered him not a word.

“If ye possess a proof greater than this, bring it forth.” The invitation to compare assumes that claims can be tested. The First Letter of John: believe not every spirit, but try the spirits whether they are of God.

“Weigh what thou hast against what hath appeared from Him.” Descartes made weighing his first rule: never to accept anything for true which I did not clearly know to be such. Is the weighing the readings ask for the same act as his?
“Behold ye the Balance and Testimony of God, not what ye possess.” Paul: the world by wisdom knew not God.
Verses “a single letter of which” none can equal. The Qur’án on its own weight: if We had caused this Qur’án to descend upon a mountain, thou verily hadst seen it humbled, rent asunder.
“The proof has been perfected, the favor completed.” The Qur’án uses the same pair of words: this day have I perfected your religion for you and completed My favour unto you.
“War not against Him Who hath come unto you with all the signs.” Gamaliel to the council in Jerusalem: if it be of God, ye cannot overthrow it; lest haply ye be found even to fight against God.

“If ye seek clear proofs, they have appeared.” Asked for a sign from heaven, Jesus sighed deeply and refused: there shall no sign be given unto this generation. Why is the demand refused in one place and met in the other, or is it the same answer?
“Mankind needs a universal educator.” Paul: the law was our schoolmaster to bring us unto Christ.

The elite who say they need no education are like officers who want no commander. The Buddha’s last counsel to his monks points the other way: be ye lamps unto yourselves; betake yourselves to no external refuge. Can a person be taught and still be his own lamp?

Humanity needs Educators from outside itself. Emerson told a class of future ministers that Jesus taught each soul’s own divinity and that the churches had turned him into an exception: the word Miracle, as pronounced by Christian churches, is Monster. What do the readings keep that Emerson gives up?
“Can anyone stand with Him in the arena of proof?” The council facing two fishermen: they perceived that they were unlearned and ignorant men, and they marvelled.
“Every proof hath bowed down before the proof of God.” Isaiah: to whom then will ye liken me, or shall I be equal? saith the Holy One.
Verses sent down “that perchance the people may attain certitude.” John ends his Gospel on the same purpose: these are written, that ye might believe.

“Is there any doubt concerning Him? Nay.” Tennyson, mourning a friend who had struggled with belief: there lives more faith in honest doubt, believe me, than in half the creeds. Is there a doubt that the readings would respect?
No doubt, no uncertainty. Thomas doubted, was shown the wounds, and was told: be not faithless, but believing; blessed are they that have not seen, and yet have believed. Was Thomas wrong to ask?
God “hath broken the seal of the choice Wine.” Isaiah on the state before: the vision of all is become unto you as the words of a book that is sealed.

Classes where the young learn “all the divine proofs.” The First Letter of Peter: be ready always to give an answer to every man that asketh you a reason of the hope that is in you, with meekness and fear.
Gatherings where seekers hear “reasoned arguments and conclusive proofs.” Paul’s habit in every town: he reasoned with them out of the scriptures.

Seekers are to hear proofs. Pascal on how conviction actually comes: people are generally better persuaded by the reasons which they have themselves discovered. How can a meeting present proofs and still leave room for that?

“If their task is to be confined to good conduct and advice, nothing will be accomplished.” The First Letter of Peter hopes for exactly that kind of persuasion: that they may without the word be won by the conversation of their wives. When does conduct speak, and when must someone speak?
They must “expound the proofs, set forth clear arguments.” Isaiah gives the invitation in God’s own voice: come now, and let us reason together.

john-herein-is-a-marvellous-thing.text: Why herein is a marvellous thing, that ye know not from whence he is, and yet he hath opened mine eyes. Now we know that God heareth not sinners: but if any man be a worshipper of God, and doeth his will, him he heareth. Since the world began was it not heard that any man opened the eyes of one that was born blind. If this man were not of God, he could do nothing

isaiah-bring-forth-your-strong-reasons.text: Produce your cause, saith the Lord; bring forth your strong reasons, saith the King of Jacob

john-what-sign-shewest-thou.text: What sign shewest thou then, that we may see, and believe thee? what dost thou work

matthew-come-down-from-the-cross.text: Likewise also the chief priests mocking him, with the scribes and elders, said, He saved others; himself he cannot save. If he be the King of Israel, let him now come down from the cross, and we will believe him

acts-not-done-in-a-corner.text: For the king knoweth of these things, before whom also I speak freely: for I am persuaded that none of these things are hidden from him; for this thing was not done in a corner

john-works-bear-witness-of-me.text: But I have greater witness than that of John: for the works which the Father hath given me to finish, the same works that I do, bear witness of me, that the Father hath sent me

luke-herod-hoped-to-have-seen-some-mirac.text: And when Herod saw Jesus, he was exceeding glad: for he was desirous to see him of a long season, because he had heard many things of him; and he hoped to have seen some miracle done by him. Then he questioned with him in many words; but he answered him nothing

quran-naught-hindereth-us-from-sending-p.text: Naught hindereth Us from sending portents save that the folk of old denied them. And We gave Thamud the she-camel - a clear portent save to warn.

quran-thou-art-a-warner-only.text: Those who disbelieve say: If only some portent were sent down upon him from his Lord! Thou art a warner only, and for every folk a guide.

quran-why-doth-not-allah-speak-unto-us.text: And those who have no knowledge say: Why doth not Allah speak unto us, or some sign come unto us? Even thus, as they now speak, spake those (who were) before them. Their hearts are all alike. We have made clear the revelations for people who are sure.

quran-invented-it-then-bring-ten-surahs.text: Or they say: He hath invented it. Say: Then bring ten surahs, the like thereof, invented, and call on everyone ye can beside Allah, if ye are truthful!
